claim: Spec §11.5 (spec.md:8785) says the recording is 'one small allocation per drained batch, plus the values boxed into that allocation'. `_record!` allocates the entries vector and the `TraceBatch` record, two allocations, plus one per touched entry, and the batches vector grows
why: Probe: `_record!` with one touched position makes 3 allocations (96 bytes), and with three it makes 5. That is the entries vector, which Julia 1.13 allocates as two objects (Array plus Memory, matching a bare `Vector{Pair{Int,Any}}(undef,1)` = 2), plus one box per value. `Base.allocatedinline(TraceBatch)` is true, so the record costs no allocation of its own, and `push!` into a size-hinted `batches` allocates nothing (amortized growth). This matches spec.md:8784-8786's one vector plus boxed values, and the claim's "two allocations, TraceBatch included" is refuted. On 1.13 that one vector counts as two runtime allocations.
